sections.title: Setting
sections.text: Utqiagvik sits at about 3 m above sea level, in a basin that runs from about 0 m to 90 m. It lies in the Arctic coastal tundra ecoregion.

sections.title: Climate
sections.text: Across the surrounding basin of about 4,662 km², rainfall averages about 134 mm a year, clearly seasonal, with August the wettest month. Temperatures there average -11.3 °C, from -26.8 °C in February to 6.1 °C in July. Of the four basins that meet here, it receives the least precipitation. Compared with the three basins around it, its basin is cooler than two and is more arid than two.

sections.title: Water
sections.text: The basin meets the sea at its outlet, so little water arrives from upstream. Lakes cover about 14% of the basin and wetlands about 67%. The basin drains directly to the sea.

sections.title: Land and geology
sections.text: Across the basin, the land is very gently sloping on average (a mean slope of 1.4%), with topsoil that averages 48% sand, 36% silt and 16% clay (USDA texture class: loam). The underlying rock is mostly siliciclastic sedimentary rocks. Permafrost underlies about 97% of it.

sections.title: Land cover around 2000
sections.text: Around 2000, neither cropland nor pasture is recorded; in the GLC2000 land cover map, the commonest class is sparse herbaceous or sparse shrub cover, at about 81%.

sections.title: Surroundings
sections.text: Utqiagvik's basin is one of four that meet here. None of them drains into it. It drains into none of them. The basins across its divides are all higher. Of the four basins that meet here, it has the lowest mean elevation, the least relief and the gentlest slopes.

sections.title: About these figures
sections.text: The elevation and ecoregion under Setting are for Utqiagvik itself. The other figures describe the basin of about 4,662 km² that contains it, from global datasets. Elevation and distances are measured from the place's point in WHG, which may be the centre of a town rather than its shore or riverbank.
